audit_findings.title: The negative anchor may perpetuate a nonrecurring Genesis bankruptcy loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $63.9 million pre-tax charge, equal to 151% of the $42.3 million negative anchor; post-tax OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The charge reduces 2025 OE and, through the latest-actual anchor, is projected through the explicit period and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In conjunction with recording the allowance for Genesis receivables, the Company recognized bad debt expense of $ 63.9 million during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The Genesis charge is demonstrated, while its retention in the OE calculation is unresolved. Adding back the filed charge before tax would move the anchor from negative $42.3 million to positive $21.6 million before other normalization and tax effects, so it can reverse the sign of operating value and change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE line by line to the $63.9 million charge, establish a sustainable credit-loss baseline from non-Genesis experience, tax-effect the adjustment, and rerun every scenario with the corrected anchor.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may add captive-insurance assets that are not excess common-equity cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.4 million bridge add-back at issue; filed captive marketable securities were $77.405 million and accrued insurance claims were $64.743 million at June 30, 2026; exact overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-distributable captive assets included as stakes or excess cash inflate the equity bridge unless associated insurance claims, collateral requirements and regulatory capital are recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: These assets are held by the Company’s wholly-owned captive insurance company subsidiary as required by state insurance regulations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that marketable securities are held by the captive and that $36.089 million is explicitly restricted, but the record does not map the $61.4 million stakes_net balance to those securities. The possible bridge overstatement is significant, but its existence and amount cannot be established from the supplied component labels.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 bridge ledger by account and legal entity; identify captive, restricted and pledged balances; reconcile them to insurance claims and the $32 million letters of credit; then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable net assets.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation funding could be assigned to common equity without its matching liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.429 million funding asset and $61.429 million matching liability at June 30, 2026; gross inclusion overstates value by about $61.4 million or $0.83 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding deferred-compensation funding to the equity bridge without its equal participant liability assigns employee assets to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: These investments represent the amounts held on behalf of the participating employees as changes in the value of these investments affect the amount of our deferred compensation liability.
audit_findings.explanation: This is strongly demonstrated: the $61.4 million stakes_net amount rounds to the filed deferred-compensation plan assets, while current and long-term deferred-compensation liabilities total the identical $61.429 million. The economic net asset is zero. The error equals about 27% of the $226.1 million stated bridge and materially misstates the bridge, even though correcting it alone would further reduce the already-negative scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Trace stakes_net to the deferred-compensation accounts, replace any gross funding amount with funding less current and long-term plan liabilities, and rerun the equity bridge and per-share values.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain exceptional ERC economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.2 million operating credit, $5.3 million interest income, $2.1 million associated fees and $12.277 million deferred ERC liability; net tax-adjusted OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: ERC income and related costs affect anchor OE, while an unnetted deferred ERC liability can overstate excess cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized $ 34.2 million of ERC refunds as a reduction to Costs of services provided , $ 5.3 million of interest income on such refunds received within Investment and other income, net , and $ 2.1 million of professional fees expense associated with the ERC refunds within Selling, general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional ERC amounts are demonstrated, but their treatment in the OE worksheet is unresolved. The $34.2 million operating credit alone equals 81% of the absolute negative anchor, so asymmetric normalization could materially change sustainable OE. The unusual permanent tax treatment prevents a reliable net adjustment without the underlying calculation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each ERC credit, interest, fee and tax entry to OE; remove nonrecurring income, restore directly associated expenses consistently, normalize taxes, verify the portfolio-income purge, net the $12.277 million liability from distributable cash, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Repeated favorable insurance-reserve releases may overstate sustainable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Favorable releases of $13.6 million in 2025, $11.6 million in 2024 and $12.5 million in 2023; the 2025 amount equals 32% of the absolute $42.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Prior-period reserve-development gains reduce current insurance expense and therefore increase anchor OE and all projected operating and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, self-insurance liabilities decreased due to favorable $ 13.6 million adjustments after considering updated actuarial estimates for projected incurred losses on past claims.
audit_findings.explanation: The releases and their three-year recurrence are demonstrated; whether the OE series normalized them is unresolved. Their consistent size makes them economically significant, but recurrence alone does not establish that favorable prior-year development is sustainable. Removing or normalizing $13.6 million of annual earnings can materially affect an anchor already dominated by exceptional items.
audit_findings.action: Obtain actuarial triangles separating current-year incurred losses from prior-year development, reconcile both components to OE, establish a defensible long-run current-claim cost, and rerun the valuation without unsupported reserve-development gains.

audit_findings.title: Pending litigation creates an unquantified claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued or underinsured settlements would reduce future OE or require a direct deduction from the common-equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, the Company is unable to reasonably estimate possible losses or form a judgment that an unfavorable outcome is either probable, reasonably possible or remote with respect to certain pending litigation claims asserted.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of pending claims and the absence of an estimable loss are demonstrated, but neither probability nor exposure is available. This is a present contingent claim rather than merely a forward-looking operating risk; the supplied record cannot establish whether it is material or already covered by accruals or insurance.
audit_findings.action: Review current litigation dockets, counsel letters, claimed damages, existing accruals, insurance limits and deductibles, and post-June developments; apply a probability-weighted bridge deduction or explicit scenario once a supportable exposure range is available.
